Definition: from G5384 and G4680; fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher":--philosopher.
BiblicalUsage: Philosophos is a philosopher, a lover of wisdom, and it appears once, at Athens. Certain philosophers of the Epicureans and of the Stoicks encounter Paul, and some call him a babbler while others say he seems to be a setter forth of strange gods.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the philosophers' charge is the gospel's compliment: they called Paul a babbler because he preached Jesus and the resurrection, and Athens had never heard anything like it.
